key_insight: Odd (Hall) viscosity can emerge self-consistently in active chiral films because shear reorients anchored torque-exerting particles, creating a transverse stress response.
engineering_relevance: This provides a microscopic route to design and tune nonreciprocal surface rheology in active coatings, bacterial carpets, and other chiral biointerfaces.
method: Built a kinetic theory for the orientational dynamics of elongated particles tethered to a no-slip surface.
Derived the shear-stress response under imposed flow and obtained the odd-viscosity tensor in closed form.
Solved the nonlinear theory numerically to capture strong-shear saturation and departure from linear response.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports analytical derivation plus numerical nonlinear solutions showing flow-aligned polarization and saturation of transverse traction at strong shear.
watch_item: The formulation is specific to idealized anchored active chiral films, so quantitative use in real systems may depend strongly on boundary conditions, particle anchoring, and finite-shear nonlinearities.
paper_title: Emergent odd response in active chiral films
